units.summary: ParseQuantity now calls CacheString on the fast int64 path and on the slow inf.Dec path before returning. The result carries a pre-populated canonical string.
units.headline: ParseQuantity now pre-caches canonical string on returned Quantity
units.reason: Changes the internal state of every parsed Quantity, which affects equality comparisons and encoding.
focus: Every return path in ParseQuantity caches the string, including the early return with the str field
Parsed Quantities now differ under reflect.DeepEqual from ones built with NewQuantity

units.summary: String no longer writes the computed string back to the receiver. It returns the cached value if present and otherwise recomputes on every call. This removes a data race on concurrent String calls, but it makes uncached Quantities slower.
units.headline: String() no longer mutates receiver; recomputes when uncached
units.reason: Changes the caching and mutation semantics of a widely used method, with performance and concurrency consequences.
focus: Quantities built via NewQuantity, math operations or deserialization now recompute the string on every String call
Callers relying on String() to populate q.s, such as DeepEqual in tests or JSON/proto paths

units.summary: This adds a public CacheString method. It computes the canonical string and always stores it on the receiver. Callers must own the instance.
units.headline: New public CacheString method stores canonical string on receiver
units.reason: New public API that mutates the receiver and is meant for explicit use at points where mutation is safe.
focus: Writing q.s unconditionally means calling it on a shared instance causes a race even when the string is already cached
Staleness: a cached s is not invalidated by later mutation, so check the math operations clear it

units.summary: The test now asserts that ParseQuantity sets the cached string. The earlier assertion that parsing leaves it empty and String() sets it was removed, which matches the new behavior.
units.headline: TestQuantityString expects ParseQuantity to pre-cache string
units.reason: Test expectations were changed to match new behavior, so the change needs a reviewer to confirm it is intended.
risk_signals: expectations changed to match new behavior
focus: The removed assertion that String() populates q.s is now covered by the new CacheString test

units.summary: This adds a test that CacheString populates the cached string, is idempotent, and handles a nil receiver.
units.headline: Adds test for CacheString behavior
units.reason: New test only.
